title: Why like terms combine
thesis: Like terms add because they count the same thing: two tiles of area x² and three more make five tiles of area x².
prerequisites: Area of a square is side times side

chapters.title: LIKE TERMS
chapters.learning_goal: Explain 2x² + 3x² = 5x² with area tiles and the distributive law.

beats.narration: Why does two x squared plus three x squared equal five x squared? Let's make the symbols visible.
beats.visual: Show the question 2x² + 3x² = 5x² as symbols waiting to be explained.

beats.narration: Take a square with side length x, where x is positive. Its area is x squared.
beats.visual: Draw one square of side x and label its area x².

beats.narration: Here are two such squares, and three more. Every tile has exactly the same area: x squared.
beats.visual: Lay out a group of two identical tiles and a group of three more.

beats.narration: Bring them together. Count five identical tiles. We changed how many we collected, not the area of each tile.
beats.visual: Slide the two groups together and count five identical tiles.

beats.narration: So, two x squared plus three x squared is two plus three, times x squared. That is five x squared.
This is the distributive law. Add the coefficients, and keep the shared variable part unchanged. The identity holds for every real x.
beats.visual: State the rule: add the coefficients, keep the shared variable part.

beats.narration: Addition keeps these terms as x squared. Multiplying x squared by x squared is different: that gives x to the fourth.
beats.visual: Contrast adding x² + x² with multiplying x² · x² = x⁴.

beats.narration: Your turn. What is four x squared plus two x squared? Explain what changes, and what stays the same.
beats.visual: Pose 4x² + 2x² and hold for the viewer to answer.

beats.narration: Six x squared. Four plus two gives six; x squared stays unchanged. Like terms combine because their variable parts match.
beats.visual: Reveal 6x² and restate why like terms combine.
